rules: A 'payment' whose type is not stated is a card payment (not a transfer). An unqualified 'transaction' or 'transfer' still in progress or not yet posted is a pending transfer.
A transfer 'from my UK account' or from another bank account is money coming into this account.

A complaint that the exchange rate the customer got was wrong, bad, or worse than expected (they got less than expected), including for an exchange in the app, is card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate, or wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal when it concerns cash received; This includes thinking the charges for a currency exchange they made are not right. exchange_charge is for asking how much exchanging costs; exchange_rate is only for neutral questions about what the rates are or where they come from.

When the customer's complaint is that their balance has not updated (and no cheque or cash deposit is mentioned), it is balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer; when it is about the transfer itself not having completed, it is pending_transfer.
A card payment that was cancelled, refused by the merchant, or reversed after it was made is reverted_card_payment?; declined_card_payment is when the card is declined at the moment of paying.
Read obvious typos by meaning (e.g. 'pop-up' or 'top-pu' means top-up).
A small unexplained charge on the statement, such as a 1 pound/dollar/euro charge, is extra_charge_on_statement, even when it shows as pending or is called a purchase.
Money the customer 'deposited' is a cheque or cash deposit, not a top-up or transfer.

When the customer is trying to make a transfer and is told it is not possible or not allowed, cannot do it, or attempts keep being unsuccessful, it is beneficiary_not_allowed. When they report getting an error message while making a transfer or payment (e.g. a large payment such as for a flat or mortgage), or that the transfer failed, it is failed_transfer. declined_transfer is a transfer reported as declined.
Doubting whether a top-up worked at all is top_up_failed; waiting for a top-up to arrive ('yet', 'taking long', 'still pending') is pending_top_up.
Using a card to top up and then finding the money is gone is topping_up_by_card.
Questions about SWIFT transfers (whether they can be used, received or cost anything) are top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge.
A virtual card that was ordered but hasn't appeared yet is getting_virtual_card (card_arrival is for physical cards in the post).

When the customer asks in general what ways they can add money to their own account, it is transfer_into_account. Asking which payment methods, card types or currencies are accepted for adding money is supported_cards_and_currencies. Other people sending money to the customer is receiving_money.
A specific cash withdrawal the customer didn't make is cash_withdrawal_not_recognised, even when they suspect their card was copied.

An unknown or unrecognised charge, without mention of a small fixed amount like 1 pound/dollar, is card_payment_not_recognised; extra_charge_on_statement is for small extra charges or fees on the statement.
Whether the customer can get a card or use the service given where they live is country_support.
Being unable to get cash out of an ATM (the ATM wouldn't work for them, card won't work at the ATM) is declined_cash_withdrawal; atm_support is about which or where ATMs can be used.
When the customer says money they sent to a friend, person or business hasn't arrived or gone through yet, it is transfer_not_received_by_recipient, even if they also ask how long transfers take.

Complaints that a specific transfer or transaction is still pending, not yet posted, or taking forever (including 'how long will my transfer stay pending?' and 'when will the transaction post?') are pending_transfer. Asking how much longer they have to wait for a transfer, or when it will reach their account, is transfer_timing, even if it has been a couple of days.
Questions about how much exchanging currency costs, including discounts or better rates for frequent exchanges, are exchange_charge.
Asking whether or how a specific card brand (e.g. American Express) can be used to add money is supported_cards_and_currencies.
A question about fees for adding money to the account, when the method is not stated, is top_up_by_card_charge.
Being charged a (higher) fee for doing banking or using the account abroad is transfer_fee_charged.
Any question about exchange rates for getting or withdrawing cash, or about withdrawing cash from an ATM while in another country without extra cost, is wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal.
Finding a card that was lost and asking whether it can still be used is card_linking.
Being charged a hidden or unexplained fee is card_payment_fee_charged; asking whether they will get extra charges is transfer_fee_charged.
Any question about auto top-up, including its limits, is automatic_top_up.
Asking whether a card can be mailed, shipped or delivered to a particular country or region is country_support.
A purchase the customer paid for that has now disappeared from the account, or that the seller says didn't go through after paying, is reverted_card_payment?.

When the customer asks when they can expect a card they ordered, even if it is late, it is card_delivery_estimate; card_arrival is reporting that the card hasn't arrived or asking to track it, without asking for an expected date.
Reactivating a card is card_linking.

instructions.question: Classify the customer's support message into the one intent it belongs to. Consider what the customer actually needs help with.
rules: A 'payment' whose type is not stated is a card payment (not a transfer). An unqualified 'transaction' or 'transfer' still in progress or not yet posted is a pending transfer.
A transfer 'from my UK account' or from another bank account is money coming into this account.

A complaint that the exchange rate the customer got was wrong, bad, or worse than expected (they got less than expected), including for an exchange in the app, is card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate, or wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal when it concerns cash received; This includes thinking the charges for a currency exchange they made are not right. exchange_charge is for asking how much exchanging costs; exchange_rate is only for neutral questions about what the rates are or where they come from.

When the customer's complaint is that their balance has not updated (and no cheque or cash deposit is mentioned), it is balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer; when it is about the transfer itself not having completed, it is pending_transfer.
A card payment that was cancelled, refused by the merchant, or reversed after it was made is reverted_card_payment?; declined_card_payment is when the card is declined at the moment of paying.
Read obvious typos by meaning (e.g. 'pop-up' or 'top-pu' means top-up).
A small unexplained charge on the statement, such as a 1 pound/dollar/euro charge, is extra_charge_on_statement, even when it shows as pending or is called a purchase.
Money the customer 'deposited' is a cheque or cash deposit, not a top-up or transfer.

When the customer is trying to make a transfer and is told it is not possible or not allowed, cannot do it, or attempts keep being unsuccessful, it is beneficiary_not_allowed. When they report getting an error message while making a transfer or payment (e.g. a large payment such as for a flat or mortgage), or that the transfer failed, it is failed_transfer. declined_transfer is a transfer reported as declined.
Doubting whether a top-up worked at all is top_up_failed; waiting for a top-up to arrive ('yet', 'taking long', 'still pending') is pending_top_up.
Using a card to top up and then finding the money is gone is topping_up_by_card.
Questions about SWIFT transfers (whether they can be used, received or cost anything) are top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge.
A virtual card that was ordered but hasn't appeared yet is getting_virtual_card (card_arrival is for physical cards in the post).

When the customer asks in general what ways they can add money to their own account, it is transfer_into_account. Asking which payment methods, card types or currencies are accepted for adding money is supported_cards_and_currencies. Other people sending money to the customer is receiving_money.
A specific cash withdrawal the customer didn't make is cash_withdrawal_not_recognised, even when they suspect their card was copied.

An unknown or unrecognised charge, without mention of a small fixed amount like 1 pound/dollar, is card_payment_not_recognised; extra_charge_on_statement is for small extra charges or fees on the statement.
Whether the customer can get a card or use the service given where they live is country_support.
Being unable to get cash out of an ATM (the ATM wouldn't work for them, card won't work at the ATM) is declined_cash_withdrawal; atm_support is about which or where ATMs can be used.
When the customer says money they sent to a friend, person or business hasn't arrived or gone through yet, it is transfer_not_received_by_recipient, even if they also ask how long transfers take.

Complaints that a specific transfer or transaction is still pending, not yet posted, or taking forever (including 'how long will my transfer stay pending?' and 'when will the transaction post?') are pending_transfer. Asking how much longer they have to wait for a transfer, or when it will reach their account, is transfer_timing, even if it has been a couple of days.
Questions about how much exchanging currency costs, including discounts or better rates for frequent exchanges, are exchange_charge.
Asking whether or how a specific card brand (e.g. American Express) can be used to add money is supported_cards_and_currencies.
A question about fees for adding money to the account, when the method is not stated, is top_up_by_card_charge.
Being charged a (higher) fee for doing banking or using the account abroad is transfer_fee_charged.
Any question about exchange rates for getting or withdrawing cash, or about withdrawing cash from an ATM while in another country without extra cost, is wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal.
Finding a card that was lost and asking whether it can still be used is card_linking.
Being charged a hidden or unexplained fee is card_payment_fee_charged; asking whether they will get extra charges is transfer_fee_charged.
Any question about auto top-up, including its limits, is automatic_top_up.
Asking whether a card can be mailed, shipped or delivered to a particular country or region is country_support.
A purchase the customer paid for that has now disappeared from the account, or that the seller says didn't go through after paying, is reverted_card_payment?.

When the customer asks when they can expect a card they ordered, even if it is late, it is card_delivery_estimate; card_arrival is reporting that the card hasn't arrived or asking to track it, without asking for an expected date.
Reactivating a card is card_linking.

A complaint that the exchange rate the customer got was wrong, bad, or worse than expected (they got less than expected), including for an exchange in the app, is card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate, or wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal when it concerns cash received; This includes thinking the charges for a currency exchange they made are not right. exchange_charge is for asking how much exchanging costs; exchange_rate is only for neutral questions about what the rates are or where they come from.

When the customer's complaint is that their balance has not updated (and no cheque or cash deposit is mentioned), it is balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer; when it is about the transfer itself not having completed, it is pending_transfer.
A card payment that was cancelled, refused by the merchant, or reversed after it was made is reverted_card_payment?; declined_card_payment is when the card is declined at the moment of paying.
Read obvious typos by meaning (e.g. 'pop-up' or 'top-pu' means top-up).
A small unexplained charge on the statement, such as a 1 pound/dollar/euro charge, is extra_charge_on_statement, even when it shows as pending or is called a purchase.
Money the customer 'deposited' is a cheque or cash deposit, not a top-up or transfer.

When the customer is trying to make a transfer and is told it is not possible or not allowed, cannot do it, or attempts keep being unsuccessful, it is beneficiary_not_allowed. When they report getting an error message while making a transfer or payment (e.g. a large payment such as for a flat or mortgage), or that the transfer failed, it is failed_transfer. declined_transfer is a transfer reported as declined.
Doubting whether a top-up worked at all is top_up_failed; waiting for a top-up to arrive ('yet', 'taking long', 'still pending') is pending_top_up.
Using a card to top up and then finding the money is gone is topping_up_by_card.
Questions about SWIFT transfers (whether they can be used, received or cost anything) are top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge.
A virtual card that was ordered but hasn't appeared yet is getting_virtual_card (card_arrival is for physical cards in the post).

When the customer asks in general what ways they can add money to their own account, it is transfer_into_account. Asking which payment methods, card types or currencies are accepted for adding money is supported_cards_and_currencies. Other people sending money to the customer is receiving_money.
A specific cash withdrawal the customer didn't make is cash_withdrawal_not_recognised, even when they suspect their card was copied.

An unknown or unrecognised charge, without mention of a small fixed amount like 1 pound/dollar, is card_payment_not_recognised; extra_charge_on_statement is for small extra charges or fees on the statement.
Whether the customer can get a card or use the service given where they live is country_support.
Being unable to get cash out of an ATM (the ATM wouldn't work for them, card won't work at the ATM) is declined_cash_withdrawal; atm_support is about which or where ATMs can be used.
When the customer says money they sent to a friend, person or business hasn't arrived or gone through yet, it is transfer_not_received_by_recipient, even if they also ask how long transfers take.

Complaints that a specific transfer or transaction is still pending, not yet posted, or taking forever (including 'how long will my transfer stay pending?' and 'when will the transaction post?') are pending_transfer. Asking how much longer they have to wait for a transfer, or when it will reach their account, is transfer_timing, even if it has been a couple of days.
Questions about how much exchanging currency costs, including discounts or better rates for frequent exchanges, are exchange_charge.
Asking whether or how a specific card brand (e.g. American Express) can be used to add money is supported_cards_and_currencies.
A question about fees for adding money to the account, when the method is not stated, is top_up_by_card_charge.
Being charged a (higher) fee for doing banking or using the account abroad is transfer_fee_charged.
Any question about exchange rates for getting or withdrawing cash, or about withdrawing cash from an ATM while in another country without extra cost, is wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal.
Finding a card that was lost and asking whether it can still be used is card_linking.
Being charged a hidden or unexplained fee is card_payment_fee_charged; asking whether they will get extra charges is transfer_fee_charged.
Any question about auto top-up, including its limits, is automatic_top_up.
Asking whether a card can be mailed, shipped or delivered to a particular country or region is country_support.
A purchase the customer paid for that has now disappeared from the account, or that the seller says didn't go through after paying, is reverted_card_payment?.

When the customer asks when they can expect a card they ordered, even if it is late, it is card_delivery_estimate; card_arrival is reporting that the card hasn't arrived or asking to track it, without asking for an expected date.
Reactivating a card is card_linking.

criteria.balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer: Money transferred into the customer's account by bank transfer has not appeared in the balance yet. A transfer from the customer's UK account or other bank that is not showing up yet, even if they ask how long it takes. Any complaint that the balance has not been updated or is taking long to update, when no cheque or cash deposit is mentioned. E.g. 'What's the time frame for a UK account transfer? I just made one and it's not showing up anywhere.'
criteria.beneficiary_not_allowed: Cannot add a beneficiary/payee/recipient, or the beneficiary is not allowed or rejected. Includes trying to transfer money and being unable to: it won't go through after several attempts, or they cannot send to a particular account.
criteria.cancel_transfer: Wants to cancel, stop or reverse a transfer they made (e.g. sent to the wrong account by mistake).
criteria.declined_transfer: A transfer the customer tried to make was declined or rejected.
criteria.failed_transfer: A transfer the customer made failed or didn't go through. A transfer reported as failed, or an error message appearing when trying to make a transfer or a large payment (e.g. for a flat or mortgage).
criteria.pending_transfer: A transfer the customer sent is still pending. A transfer or transaction the customer made that has not completed, posted or shown up on their dashboard yet. Includes a pending transaction taking long to post or clear. Includes complaining that a specific transfer (e.g. an international one) is taking forever. Includes asking how long their transfer will stay pending. Includes an urgent transfer that finally worked out (was submitted) but that they have been waiting on for a long time, asking how long to expect to wait.
criteria.transfer_fee_charged: Was charged a fee for making a transfer. Includes being charged a higher fee for banking abroad, and asking whether they will get extra charges.
criteria.transfer_into_account: How to transfer money into the account (add money by bank transfer); account details for incoming transfers. Includes the customer asking in general which ways or methods they can use to add money to their own account.
criteria.transfer_not_received_by_recipient: The customer sent money but the recipient has not received it. Includes money sent to a friend or retailer that hasn't arrived or gone through yet, even if they ask how long it takes.
criteria.transfer_timing: How long transfers take to arrive; transfer processing times. General questions about transfer durations; also 'when can I expect my transfer to reach my account?' or 'it's been a couple days, how much longer do I have to wait for my transfer?'.
criteria.receiving_money: How to receive money from others, get paid, or receive a salary into the account. Includes how other people can send, transfer or top up money to the customer.
